concepts.title: Geographical Expanse and Territorial Extent of India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Geographical Expanse and Territorial Extent of India' refers to.
questions.a: The total spatial expanse of India covering its geographical surface area along with north-to-south and east-to-west linear dimensions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Geographical Expanse and Territorial Extent of India'.
questions.a: India covers about 3.28 million square kilometers with distinct latitudinal and longitudinal boundaries.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Geographical Expanse and Territorial Extent of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: OUR COUNTRY - INDIA (source: fess207.txt lines 1-20)

questions.q: Calculate local time difference for longitudinal difference of {degree_diff} degrees. Use the method 'Longitudinal Time Difference Calculation'. Work with: degree_diff = 45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of time_diff_hr.
questions.a: 3 units

questions.q: Find time gap in hours between two longitudes separated by {degree_diff} degrees. Use the method 'Longitudinal Time Difference Calculation'. Work with: degree_diff = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of time_diff_hr.
questions.a: 0.2667 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Longitudinal Time Difference Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: Computation of local time variation between two longitudes based on the constant rate of four minutes per degree of longitudinal separation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Longitudinal Time Difference Calculation'.
questions.a: Earth rotation causes a local time change of four minutes for each degree of longitude.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Longitudinal Time Difference Calculation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: time_diff_min = degree_diff * 4

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Locational Setting and Latitudinal-Longitudinal Boundaries' refers to.
questions.a: The precise global coordinates defining the mainland of India in the northern and eastern hemispheres, including key latitude lines.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Locational Setting and Latitudinal-Longitudinal Boundaries'.
questions.a: India lies in the Northern and Eastern Hemispheres, bisected by the Tropic of Cancer at 23 degrees 30 minutes N.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Locational Setting and Latitudinal-Longitudinal Boundaries' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: LOCATIONAL SETTING (source: fess207.txt lines 20-35)

concepts.title: India's Land Neighbours and Marine Boundaries

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India's Land Neighbours and Marine Boundaries' refers to.
questions.a: The geographical relationships of India with adjacent countries sharing land borders or maritime boundaries across surrounding seas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India's Land Neighbours and Marine Boundaries'.
questions.a: Seven countries border India by land while island neighbours lie across water channels such as the Palk Strait.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India's Land Neighbours and Marine Boundaries' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: INDIA'S NEIGHBOURS (source: fess207.txt lines 45-65)

concepts.title: Political and Administrative Structure of India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Political and Administrative Structure of India' refers to.
questions.a: The governance framework dividing India into states created primarily on a linguistic basis and centrally governed union territories.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Political and Administrative Structure of India'.
questions.a: India comprises 28 states and 8 union territories with New Delhi as the national capital.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Political and Administrative Structure of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: POLITICAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE DIVISIONS (source: fess207.txt lines 65-75)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Himalayan Mountain Range Structure' refers to.
questions.a: The northernmost mountain barrier of India, divided into three parallel structural longitudinal zones.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Himalayan Mountain Range Structure'.
questions.a: The Himalayas consist of Himadri (Great Himalayas), Himachal (Middle Himalayas), and Shiwalik (Outer Himalayas).

questions.q: Under which section is 'Himalayan Mountain Range Structure' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: PHYSICAL DIVISIONS (source: fess207.txt lines 75-90)

concepts.title: Northern Indian Plains and Alluvial River Systems

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Northern Indian Plains and Alluvial River Systems' refers to.
questions.a: Flat and fertile plains located south of the Himalayas formed by silt deposits carried by major river networks.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Northern Indian Plains and Alluvial River Systems'.
questions.a: Fine alluvial soil brought by the Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra and tributaries creates highly fertile, densely populated plains.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Northern Indian Plains and Alluvial River Systems' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: PHYSICAL DIVISIONS (source: fess207.txt lines 90-105)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Peninsular Plateau and Relief Features' refers to.
questions.a: A triangular elevated landform with uneven terrain south of the northern plains, rich in mineral resources and framed by hill ranges.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Peninsular Plateau and Relief Features'.
questions.a: The plateau is bounded by Aravali, Vindhya, Satpura ranges and drained westward by Narmada and Tapi rivers into the Arabian Sea.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Peninsular Plateau and Relief Features' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: PHYSICAL DIVISIONS (source: fess207.txt lines 105-130)

concepts.title: Coastal Plains, Deltas, and Island Archipelagos

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Coastal Plains, Deltas, and Island Archipelagos' refers to.
questions.a: Coastal regions bordering the peninsular plateau along with offshore island groups formed by coral polyps or sub-sea topography.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Coastal Plains, Deltas, and Island Archipelagos'.
questions.a: Narrow western and broad eastern coastal plains, Sundarbans delta, coral Lakshadweep in Arabian Sea, and Andaman & Nicobar in Bay of Bengal.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Coastal Plains, Deltas, and Island Archipelagos' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: PHYSICAL DIVISIONS (source: fess207.txt lines 130-160)
